title: Operator local sandbox and simulation lab setup
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview

This document describes how platform operators and engineers can provision a reproducible local sandbox and simulation lab for validating LLM inference operator workflows. The lab focuses on multi-tenant traffic shaping, cache warmup/eviction, tenant burst scenarios, and safe fallbacks. Use this guide to run deterministic experiments, validate runbooks, and produce dashboard-backed evidence before rolling changes to staging/production.

Goals

- Provide an easy-to-reproduce local environment for operator training and automated experiments.
- Surface degradations that affect SLOs (tail latency, token throughput, error budget burn).
- Validate operator interventions: eviction, prefetch toggles, model variant swap, and cross-region routing simulation.
- Provide artifacts (traces, dashboards, metrics) for retrospective analysis and remediation.

Scope and intended users

- Audience: platform operators, runtime developers, SREs, and solutions engineers.
- Not intended for production data ingestion or customer-facing endpoints. Use synthetic tenants and prompts only.

Prerequisites and host requirements

1. Workstation or CI runner with Docker (20.10+) and docker-compose.
2. Optional: NVIDIA GPU + nvidia-docker2 for kernel-level performance tests (CUDA 11.8 recommended).
3. 8 CPU cores, 32 GB RAM, 100 GB disk recommended for multi-tenant simulations.
4. Git checkout of the platform-sim repo: `git clone git@internal:redwood/platform-sim.git`
5. Node 18.x or Python 3.10 for simulation harness.

Quick start (single-machine)

1. Clone and enter the repo: `git clone git@internal:redwood/platform-sim.git && cd platform-sim`
2. Build local images (CPU-only):

   ```bash
   ./scripts/build-local.sh --mode cpu
   ```

3. Bring up the sandbox:

   ```bash
   docker-compose -f docker/docker-compose.local.yml up --build -d
   ```

4. Seed synthetic tenants and prompts: `./scripts/seed-tenants.py --tenants 12 --profiles mixed-burst`
5. Start workload generator: `./tools/workload-driver run --scenario prefix-cache-stress --duration 15m`
6. Open dashboards at `http://localhost:3000` and follow the lab dashboard named "Operator Local Simulation".

Configuration matrix (example)

| Component | Minimal | Recommended | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| CPU | 4 cores | 8 cores | Run runtime containers and generator |
| RAM | 8 GB | 32 GB | Model caches and KV warmsets |
| Disk | 20 GB | 100 GB | Logs, synthetic corpora, trace storage |
| GPU | none | 1 x A10 / A100 | Kernel perf / quantization tests (optional) |

Simulation scenarios to validate

1. Cold-start storm
   - Objective: Validate warmup orchestration and prefix-KV prefetch policies.
   - Steps: seed zero cache state, run 100 tenant startups at t=0, observe cold-start SLOs.
   - Expected signals: token-latency spike, priming trafﬁc on fetcher, increased disk I/O.

2. Tenant burst with quota exhaustion
   - Objective: Test soft and hard throttles, token buydown and burst-credit reclamation.
   - Steps: configure tenant A with a 10 TPS baseline and 200 TPS burst_credit, then drive 400 TPS for 2 minutes.
   - Expected signals: fair-share reallocation, throttle counters, billing-metering events.

3. Model variant fallback misfire
   - Objective: Ensure safe fallback from GPU-quantized model to CPU variant without request loss.
   - Steps: force simulated kernel OOM on GPU node, confirm automatic reroute to compatible variant.
   - Expected signals: model-swap event, increased end-to-end latency, per-tenant error-rate remains <0.5%

4. KV cache corruption recovery
   - Objective: Validate operator runbook for partial KV prefix corruption and fallback reconstitution.
   - Steps: inject corruption into one shard; observe reconstructor behavior and eviction policies.
   - Expected signals: shard-read-errors, reconstitution job run, SLO-impact window < 5 minutes.

Operator runbook exercises (step-by-step)

1. Eviction and soft-restore
   - Trigger: prefix-cache memory exceeds 95% or eviction counter > 1000/min.
   - Procedure:
     1. Open lab dashboard and confirm memory and eviction counters.
     2. Execute: `./tools/operator evict --shard shard-3 --target 15%`
     3. Monitor: `kubectl logs -f controller-operator` and dashboard eviction events.
     4. If service errors > 1%, run: `./tools/operator prefetch --shard shard-3 --policy conservative`
     5. Annotate the incident in the lab incident diary and create a postmortem ticket if deviation persists.

2. Canary model swap and rollback
   - Trigger: operator-initiated canary to test new kernel optimizations.
   - Procedure:
     1. Deploy canary variant with `scripts/deploy-canary.sh --variant quant-kernel-v2 --percent 3`
     2. Observe trace-level quality regression (use eval prompts in `./data/eval-prompts`).
     3. If latency reduction but quality drop > 2% for key prompt set, rollback: `scripts/rollback-canary.sh`

Metrics, dashboards and alerts to monitor

- Dashboards: Operator Local Simulation (Grafana) containing panels for: prefix cache occupancy, eviction rate, per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, model-swap events, operator actions timeline.
- Prometheus metrics of interest: `runtime_prefix_cache_bytes`, `eviction_ops_total`, `tenant_p95_latency_ms`, `model_swap_count`, `operator_eviction_requests_total`
- Baseline alert thresholds (lab-focused):
  - tenant_p95_latency_ms > 750ms for > 60s
  - eviction_ops_total > 500 per minute
  - model_swap_count > 5 in 10 minutes

Automated validation harness and golden checks

- Use `./tools/validate-run --baseline ./golden/baseline-metrics.json` to compare a run to golden expectations. The validator checks: p95 latency drift, token throughput, and error-rate regressions.
- Store artifacts under `artifacts/<run-id>/` for retrospectives and reproducibility. Include: traces (zipkin), metrics snapshot (prometheus dump), and dashboard snapshot (grafana export).

Retrospective and experiment template

- Title: [short] e.g., "Simulator run 2026-02-15: prefix-cache storm"
- Hypothesis: What we expect to change and why.
- Steps: exact script commands and config used.
- Observations: numeric evidence (p95, p99, eviction counts).
- Action items: config changes, runbook updates, owner and due date.

Ownership, access and safety controls

- Lab owner: Platform Experiments Team (alias: #platform-experiments)
- Access: internal-only, restricted to SRE and runtime devs. Use temporary tokens with 8-hour TTL for external collaborators.
- Data policy: use only synthetic prompts and tenant identifiers. Never seed production PII into the lab.

Integration with CI and training

- CI: add a lightweight smoke-scenario to PR gating: `./tools/workload-driver run --scenario quick-smoke --duration 2m`
- Training: use the lab for 2-hour operator onboarding exercises; maintain a curriculum with 6 canonical scenarios.

Appendix: common troubleshooting snippets

- Recreate an eviction event locally: `./tools/workload-driver run --scenario eviction-repro --scale 8`
- Collect controller debug logs: `kubectl -n runtime logs $(kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=controller -o name)`
- Export metrics snapshot: `promtool snapshot --output artifacts/<run-id>/prom-snapshot.tar`

Contacts and escalation path

- Lab owner: Priya Patel (priya@redwood.ai)
- Platform ops on-call alias: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
- If lab environments behave inconsistently across hosts, escalate to runtime-qa (Liam Chen).

End of document
